newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss held in Zurich in Sri Lanka child abuse case.
newsitem.headline: Swiss held in Zurich in Sri Lanka child abuse case.

text.p: A Swiss man suspected of sexually abusing children in Sri Lanka was detained on Tuesday when he arrived in Zurich after the Sri Lankan government had deported him, prosecutors in Zurich said.
Zurich district attorney Peter Pellegrini said police took Viktor Baumann, 54, into custody at Zurich's airport.
"Tomorrow we will decide if he will remain in custody," he said.
Sexual abuse carries a maximum penalty of five years in prison. He could face 10 years in jail if charged and convicted of sexual coercion, Pellegrini said.
Baumann was charged in Sri Lanka with gross indecency and grave sexual abuse of children, police said.

The Zurich native and a long-time resident of Sri Lanka left on an Air Lanka flight. He is to stand trial in connection with several child sex charges in Sri Lanka, Thailand and other countries, police in Colombo said. "He is not going free. Swiss authorities are awaiting his arrival," Deputy Inspector General Mohamed Nizam told Reuters.

Baumann, a foreign investor and a resident of Sri Lanka for the past eight years, was arrested last October in the company of several local children at his house near the coastal resort of Negombo, 24 miles (38 km) north of Colombo.
He was charged with gross indecency between persons and grave sexual abuse, Nizam said.
He was remanded for two weeks and released on bail. He was due to be indicted at a local court hearing on February 26.
Police decided to deport Baumann because of charges pending against him in other countries. Baumann will be tried for all the charges in Switzerland, Nizam said.
"In Switzerland he is wanted for sexual offences, we're unsure of the exact nature of his offences in other countries," he said.

In a separate case, Nizam said police have asked immigration authorities to deport Armin Heinrich Pfaffhauser, a 58-year-old Swiss national who last week was sentenced to two years in jail for "committing an unnatural offence" on two Sri Lankan boys.
Pfaffhauser is the first foreigner to be convicted of the offence. He pleaded not guilty.
Child abuse cases are also pending against a German and a Belgian national in Sri Lankan courts. Another Swiss national, who jumped bail, is being tried in absentia.
Sri Lanka last year passed tough new laws aimed at curbing paedophile activity, said to be rampant along the tropical island's western coastal belt.
The new law calls for a minimum 10-year jail-term and a maximum 20-year sentence for pimps and their clients. It pushed the minimum age of consent up to 18 for boys and 16 for girls.
